cards.definition: **Definition.** A Markov kernel from observations to actions used when a deterministic choice cannot attain an exact testing level or decision optimum.
major_error_concepts: Adding arbitrary randomness without preserving measurability size or the declared action distribution.
cards.prompt: Define Action randomization kernel. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A Markov kernel from observations to actions used when a deterministic choice cannot attain an exact testing level or decision optimum.

cards.definition: For independent observations with likelihood L(theta)=product_i f_theta(x_i), the log likelihood is ell(theta)=sum_i log f_theta(x_i). Since log is increasing, the maximizers agree where L>0; use log 0=-infinity for zero-likelihood parameter values. A term may be dropped without changing maximizers only if it is independent of theta. Independence supplies this product form, not the act of taking logarithms.
major_error_concepts: Drop every normalization term even when it depends on theta, because logarithms make such terms irrelevant.
cards.prompt: State the additive log-likelihood identity and its parameter-dependent-term and zero-likelihood rules.
required_concepts: Log likelihood converts the independent-sample density product into a sum.
Log zero is minus infinity under the extended-value convention.
Only parameter-independent additive terms may be omitted.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A measurable map from observations to an action space evaluated by loss and risk rather than only by proximity to a scalar parameter.
major_error_concepts: Calling an informal recommendation a decision rule without an action space or loss.
cards.prompt: Define Decision rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A measurable map from observations to an action space evaluated by loss and risk rather than only by proximity to a scalar parameter.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A model whose laws all admit densities relative to one common sigma-finite measure with the chosen version and support qualifications explicit.
major_error_concepts: Treating density values as intrinsic when the dominating measure or version changes.
cards.prompt: Define Dominated statistical model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A model whose laws all admit densities relative to one common sigma-finite measure with the chosen version and support qualifications explicit.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The expected score outer product or negative expected log-likelihood Hessian under regularity with parameter sample-size and parameterization explicit.
major_error_concepts: Using observed curvature or data variance as Fisher information without the identity conditions.
cards.prompt: Define Fisher information. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The expected score outer product or negative expected log-likelihood Hessian under regularity with parameter sample-size and parameterization explicit.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The property that distinct parameter values induce distinct sampling laws for every inferentially relevant coordinate.
major_error_concepts: Reporting a unique estimate because the optimizer returned one representative.
cards.prompt: Define Identifiable statistical model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The property that distinct parameter values induce distinct sampling laws for every inferentially relevant coordinate.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The observed-sample density or mass viewed as a function of the parameter up to parameter-independent positive factors under a fixed domination convention.
major_error_concepts: Normalizing likelihood over the parameter as if it were a sampling density or prior.
cards.prompt: Define Likelihood function. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The observed-sample density or mass viewed as a function of the parameter up to parameter-independent positive factors under a fixed domination convention.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The comparison of two parameter values or restricted model maxima whose numerator denominator orientation and zero cases determine its evidence and testing role.
major_error_concepts: Reversing the ratio while keeping the same rejection inequality or calling it posterior odds.
cards.prompt: Define Likelihood-ratio object. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The comparison of two parameter values or restricted model maxima whose numerator denominator orientation
and zero cases determine its evidence and testing role.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A model coordinate needed to describe the sampling law but not itself the specified target and therefore requiring explicit conditioning profiling integration or orthogonalization.
major_error_concepts: Deleting the nuisance coordinate from the model because it is not the final estimand.
cards.prompt: Define Nuisance parameter. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A model coordinate needed to describe the sampling law but not itself the specified target
and therefore requiring explicit conditioning profiling integration or orthogonalization.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The random observation vector and its realized value kept distinct from the population law parameter and any statistic computed from it.
major_error_concepts: Treating the realized data as still random inside one fixed likelihood optimization.
cards.prompt: Define Observable sample. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The random observation vector and its realized value kept distinct from the population law parameter and any statistic computed from it.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The negative observed Hessian of log likelihood at a declared sample and parameter value rather than its expectation under repeated sampling.
major_error_concepts: Calling any optimizer Hessian Fisher information without sign scale and expectation checks.
cards.prompt: Define Observed information. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The negative observed Hessian of log likelihood at a declared sample and parameter value rather than its expectation under repeated sampling.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The set of admissible model indices including constraints boundaries nuisance coordinates and nonunique parameterizations that govern every optimization and guarantee.
major_error_concepts: Differentiating on the real line and accepting an inadmissible parameter value.
cards.prompt: Define Parameter space. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The set of admissible model indices including constraints boundaries nuisance coordinates
and nonunique parameterizations that govern every optimization and guarantee.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The parameter derivative of log likelihood under differentiability and support conditions with its random and observed versions distinguished.
major_error_concepts: Differentiating through a parameter-dependent support and invoking regular identities automatically.
cards.prompt: Define Score function. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The parameter derivative of log likelihood under differentiability and support conditions with its random and observed versions distinguished.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A measurable function of the observable sample whose value contains no unknown parameter even when its distribution depends on that parameter.
major_error_concepts: Including the unknown variance inside the formula and still calling it a statistic.
cards.prompt: Define measurable sample statistic.
required_concepts: A measurable function of the observable sample whose value contains no unknown parameter even when its distribution depends on that parameter.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The indexed family of probability laws on one measurable observation space together with the exact parameter indexing and observation contract.
major_error_concepts: Calling a dataset alone an experiment or changing the sample law between procedures.
cards.prompt: Define Statistical experiment. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The indexed family of probability laws on one measurable observation space together with the exact parameter indexing and observation contract.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The estimand defined as a function of the sampling law or parameter rather than as the observed statistic used to estimate it.
major_error_concepts: Calling the estimator itself the parameter or changing from mean to median after seeing data.
cards.prompt: Define Statistical functional target. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The estimand defined as a function of the sampling law or parameter rather than as the observed statistic used to estimate it.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The declared collection of candidate sampling laws whose carrier support parameterization and exclusions determine the inferential question.
major_error_concepts: Calling any convenient density a model without checking normalization support or scientific plausibility.
cards.prompt: Define Statistical model family. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The declared collection of candidate sampling laws whose carrier support parameterization and exclusions determine the inferential question.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A statistic whose sampling distribution is parameter-free in the specified model without implying irrelevance for precision diagnostics or conditional inference.
major_error_concepts: Calling a statistic ancillary because its observed value looks stable across bootstrap samples.
cards.prompt: Define Ancillary statistic. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: First material clause: A statistic whose sampling distribution is parameter-free in the specified model
Remaining material clause: without implying irrelevance for precision diagnostics or conditional inference.

cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It proves independence between a complete sufficient statistic and every ancillary statistic, simplifying distributional and exact-inference arguments; sufficiency without completeness is not enough.
major_error_concepts: Invoking Basu with minimal sufficiency alone or with a statistic whose law contains a nuisance parameter.
cards.prompt: What is Basu independence theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
required_concepts: It proves independence between a complete sufficient statistic and every ancillary statistic, simplifying distributional and exact-inference arguments
sufficiency without completeness is not enough.

cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** The theorem that a complete sufficient statistic is independent of every ancillary statistic under the same dominated experiment and exact definitions.
major_error_concepts: Invoking Basu with minimal sufficiency alone or with a statistic whose law contains a nuisance parameter.
cards.prompt: State Basu independence theorem, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
required_concepts: The theorem that a complete sufficient statistic is independent of every ancillary statistic under the same dominated experiment
and exact definitions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A sufficient data reduction that is a measurable function of every other sufficient reduction under the specified comparison convention.
major_error_concepts: Calling the statistic with smallest numerical dimension minimal without the ordering property.
cards.prompt: Define Coarsest parameter-preserving reduction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A sufficient data reduction that is a measurable function of every other sufficient reduction under the specified comparison convention.

cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It characterizes sufficiency by making the conditional distribution of the full data given the statistic parameter-free, clarifying exactly what information is retained; parameter-free marginal behavior of the statistic is a different idea.
major_error_concepts: Writing a formal conditional density without verifying the conditioning object and model support.
cards.prompt: What is Conditional-law characterization of sufficiency used for, and what is its main limitation?
required_concepts: It characterizes sufficiency by making the conditional distribution of the full data given the statistic parameter-free, clarifying exactly what information is retained
parameter-free marginal behavior of the statistic is a different idea.

cards.definition: In a statistical experiment where the relevant regular conditional laws exist, T(X) is sufficient exactly when there is a conditional-law kernel K(t,B), independent of theta, such that P_theta(X in B | T)=K(T,B) almost surely under each model law for every measurable B. The marginal law of T may still depend on theta; parameter-free marginal behavior is ancillarity, not sufficiency.
major_error_concepts: T is sufficient if and only if its own marginal distribution is independent of theta.
cards.prompt: State the conditional-law characterization of sufficiency, including the kernel and existence qualification.
required_concepts: Sufficiency is equivalent to a common parameter-free conditional law of X given T.
State the conditional kernel equality almost surely under each model law.
Regular-conditional-law existence is part of the stated scope.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A subfamily whose natural parameter is restricted to a lower-dimensional curved set so full-family sufficiency may remain while completeness and information geometry change.
major_error_concepts: Treating the curve coordinate as if it ranged over an open full-dimensional natural space.
cards.prompt: Define Curved exponential family. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: First material clause: A subfamily whose natural parameter is restricted to a lower-dimensional curved set so
Remaining material clause: full-family sufficiency may remain while completeness and information geometry change.

cards.definition: A canonical exponential-family form is f_eta(x)=h(x) exp{eta^T T(x)-A(eta)}, relative to a fixed measure mu, where A(eta)=log integral h(x)exp{eta^T T(x)}dmu(x). The natural parameter domain consists of eta for which this integral is finite. The base h and its support do not vary with eta in this form; eta is the natural parameter and T is the canonical statistic.
major_error_concepts: Any expression containing exp is an exponential family, and its support indicator may depend arbitrarily on eta inside h.
cards.prompt: State the canonical exponential-family density and identify its natural domain and log-partition function.
required_concepts: Give the normalized h exp(eta^T T-A) representation.
A is the log-normalizing integral and is finite on the natural domain.
The base measure and support are independent of the natural parameter.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The completeness result for a natural statistic when the natural parameter space contains an open set of full dimension under exact integrability conditions.
major_error_concepts: Calling every exponential-family statistic complete regardless of curvature or parameter-space dimension.
cards.prompt: Define Full-rank exponential-family completeness. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The completeness result for a natural statistic when the natural parameter space contains an open set of full dimension under exact integrability conditions.

cards.definition: Let X_1,...,X_n be iid with density f and CDF F. Select indices 1≤k_1<...<k_r≤n. Put k_0=0, k_(r+1)=n+1, x_0=-infinity, x_(r+1)=infinity, and nu_j=k_(j+1)-k_j-1 for j=0,...,r. On x_1<...<x_r the selected joint density is n! [product_{j=0}^r (F(x_(j+1))-F(x_j))^(nu_j)/nu_j!] [product_{j=1}^r f(x_j)], and zero otherwise, with F(-infinity)=0, F(infinity)=1 and 0^0=1. In particular all n ordered values have density n! product_i f(x_i) on the ordered region.
major_error_concepts: The joint density of all n sorted observations is product_i f(x_i) on all of R^n because sorting preserves independence.
cards.prompt: State the joint density of selected order statistics from an iid continuous sample, including the all-order-statistic special case.
required_concepts: Use iid observations with an absolutely continuous law.
Include interval counts and probabilities with the multinomial coefficient.
Include the ordered support; the all-order-statistic case reduces to n! times the density product.

cards.definition: For a dominated model with common positive support under a standard measurable minimal-sufficiency criterion, if T(x)=T(y) exactly when f_theta(x)/f_theta(y) is independent of theta, then T is minimal sufficient. Equal statistic values group proportional likelihood functions. Parameter-dependent support or zeros require a support-aware proportionality formulation or another justified theorem; they do not make every minimal-sufficiency argument impossible.
major_error_concepts: If T(x)=T(y), likelihood ratios may still vary with theta and T remains minimal sufficient.
cards.prompt: State a common-positive-support likelihood-ratio criterion for minimal sufficiency and its zero/support boundary.
required_concepts: State the iff between equal T values and parameter-independent likelihood ratios in the common-positive-support version.
Conclude minimal sufficiency, not just low dimension.
Handle zero densities or parameter-dependent support explicitly when using an extension.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The regular exponential-family results equating first and second natural-parameter derivatives to the canonical statistic mean and covariance.
major_error_concepts: Using the identities at a boundary or in a curved family without checking regularity.
cards.prompt: Define Log-partition derivative identities. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The regular exponential-family results equating first and second natural-parameter derivatives to the canonical statistic mean and covariance.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The set of canonical coordinates for which the log-partition integral is finite with openness regularity and original-parameter mapping stated.
major_error_concepts: Assuming the original parameter space and natural parameter space are identical.
cards.prompt: Define Natural-coordinate domain of an exponential family. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The set of canonical coordinates for which the log-partition integral is finite with openness regularity and original-parameter mapping stated.
cards.term: Natural-coordinate domain of an exponential family

cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It provides a practical density or mass-function test for sufficiency by isolating all parameter dependence through a statistic; support and domination conditions must be handled rather than hidden in the factorization.
major_error_concepts: Dropping a parameter-dependent support indicator into the sample-only factor.
cards.prompt: What is Neyman-Fisher factorization theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
required_concepts: It provides a practical density or mass-function test for sufficiency by isolating all parameter dependence through a statistic
support and domination conditions must be handled rather than hidden in the factorization.

cards.definition: For a dominated family on standard measurable observation/statistic spaces, T is sufficient if and only if its densities admit f_theta(x)=g_theta(T(x))h(x), up to the relevant almost-everywhere versions, with nonnegative measurable factors and h independent of theta. All parameter-dependent support restrictions must remain in g_theta(T(x)); they cannot be discarded or hidden in a sample-only h.
major_error_concepts: A parameter-dependent support indicator can be discarded from the likelihood when applying factorization.
cards.prompt: State the dominated-model Neyman-Fisher factorization theorem and explain where support indicators belong.
required_concepts: State sufficiency iff f_theta(x)=g_theta(T(x))h(x) in the dominated setting.
h is parameter-independent and the factors are measurable.
Retain parameter-dependent support indicators in the parameter/statistic factor.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The deliberate partition of observations for independent procedure stages with reduced effective sample size and changed sufficiency or risk made explicit.
major_error_concepts: Calling data splitting free protection or claiming the selected statistic is sufficient for the original full experiment.
cards.prompt: Define Sample splitting and information loss. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The deliberate partition of observations for independent procedure stages with reduced effective sample size and changed sufficiency or risk made explicit.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The indexed value in a statistically ordered sample with ties support sampling law and original observation identities distinguished.
major_error_concepts: Treating sorted sample values as independent or forgetting ties in discrete samples.
cards.prompt: Define Sorted-sample order statistic. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The indexed value in a statistically ordered sample with ties support sampling law and original observation identities distinguished.

cards.definition: Let X_1,X_2 be iid Bernoulli(p), 0<p<1, and propose T=X_1. Samples x=(0,0) and y=(0,1) have equal T but likelihood ratio (1-p)/p, which depends on p. Thus T is not sufficient for the two-observation model. Equivalently, the conditional law of X_2 given T is still Bernoulli(p). Any explicit model/summary with a verified parameter-dependent conditional or equal-summary likelihood ratio is a valid alternative witness.
major_error_concepts: The sample sum in an iid Bernoulli model is insufficient solely because it omits the original order of observations.
cards.prompt: Give and verify a concrete counterexample to a proposed statistic being sufficient.
required_concepts: Provide an explicit model and proposed data reduction.
Show its conditional law retains parameter dependence or an equal-summary likelihood ratio depends on the parameter.
Conclude failure of sufficiency using the defining property, not predictive performance alone.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The parameter-free conditional distribution of the full observation after a specified summary is fixed under the same statistical experiment.
major_error_concepts: Calling every one-to-one recoding informative but then claiming dimensional compression.
cards.prompt: Define Sufficiency of a data reduction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The parameter-free conditional distribution of the full observation after a specified summary is fixed under the same statistical experiment.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The bounded-completeness property restricting the zero-expectation implication to bounded functions and retaining its difference from integrable completeness.
major_error_concepts: Applying bounded completeness to an unbounded estimator without integrability and approximation proof.
cards.prompt: Define Zero-expectation uniqueness for bounded transforms. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The bounded-completeness property restricting the zero-expectation implication to bounded functions and retaining its difference from integrable completeness.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The completeness property that every integrable function of the specified reduction having expectation zero for all parameter values vanishes almost surely under all model laws.
major_error_concepts: Checking only linear functions or one parameter value and calling the statistic complete.
cards.prompt: Define Zero-expectation uniqueness for integrable transforms. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: First material clause: The completeness property that every integrable function of the specified reduction having
Remaining material clause: expectation zero for all parameter values vanishes almost surely under all model laws.

cards.definition: In a regular scalar model with score U, E[U]=0 and 0<I(theta)=E[U²]<infinity, let T have finite variance and differentiable mean m(theta)=E_theta[T], with differentiation allowed under expectation. Then Var_theta(T)≥[m'(theta)]²/I(theta). For estimating g(theta) with bias b=m-g, this is [(g'+b')²]/I; MSE adds b(theta)². The unbiased bound cannot simply be imposed on biased estimators.
major_error_concepts: Every biased estimator has variance at least [g'(theta)]²/I(theta), regardless of its bias derivative.
cards.prompt: State the scalar information bound for a biased estimator and express it using the bias derivative.
required_concepts: Use the derivative of the estimator mean in the variance lower bound.
For target g and bias b, the numerator is (g'+b')².
Require the regular score/interchange and finite variance/information conditions.

cards.definition: Under the regular scalar Cramer-Rao assumptions with an unbiased finite-variance T for g(theta) and 0<I(theta)<infinity, equality holds at theta exactly when T-g(theta)=[g'(theta)/I(theta)]U_theta almost surely, where U_theta is the score. This is the equality condition for Cauchy-Schwarz. Attainment at one theta is not by itself attainment throughout the model.
major_error_concepts: A variance equal to the bound at one parameter proves that the estimator attains it for every parameter.
cards.prompt: State the scalar Cramer-Rao equality condition and distinguish pointwise from model-wide attainment.
required_concepts: State the centered-estimator proportionality to the score with coefficient g'/I.
Use almost-sure equality under the model law and the regular bound assumptions.
Distinguish pointwise from uniform attainment.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An estimator commuting with a declared transformation group on samples and targets under an invariant or compatible loss.
major_error_concepts: Calling an estimator invariant when it should transform with the parameter.
cards.prompt: Define Equivariant estimator. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An estimator commuting with a declared transformation group on samples and targets under an invariant or compatible loss.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A sample-dependent equation whose root defines an estimator with unbiased score consistency and multiple-root properties separately qualified.
major_error_concepts: Calling any stationary point the unique consistent estimator.
cards.prompt: Define Estimating equation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A sample-dependent equation whose root defines an estimator with unbiased score consistency and multiple-root properties separately qualified.

cards.definition: The sampling distribution of an estimator T(X) is its probability law when the data are repeatedly drawn under a specified P_theta. It is the pushforward of the data law by T and may depend on theta and sample size. The observed estimate T(x) is a value, while an asymptotic normal approximation is not automatically its exact finite-sample law.
major_error_concepts: The sampling distribution is the posterior law of theta conditional on one fixed estimate.
cards.prompt: Define Estimator sampling distribution. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Describe the estimator law induced by repeatedly sampling the data under P_theta.
Distinguish the random estimator from its realized estimate.
Separate exact finite-sample laws from asymptotic approximations.

cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It identifies an unbiased function of a complete sufficient statistic as the unique minimum-variance unbiased estimator, converting completeness into an optimality guarantee; biased estimators and incomplete statistics lie outside the conclusion.
major_error_concepts: Invoking uniqueness from sufficiency without completeness or outside the unbiased class.
cards.prompt: What is Lehmann-Scheffe uniqueness theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
required_concepts: It identifies an unbiased function of a complete sufficient statistic as the unique minimum-variance unbiased estimator, converting completeness into an optimality guarantee
biased estimators and incomplete statistics lie outside the conclusion.

cards.definition: Let S be complete and sufficient for the model. If delta(S) is unbiased for g(theta) and has finite second moment under every model law, then it is UMVU among unbiased finite-variance estimators, and any other UMVU estimator equals it almost surely under every model law. The conclusion is within the unbiased class and does not assert minimum MSE among biased estimators.
major_error_concepts: An unbiased function of any sufficient statistic is uniquely minimum-MSE among all estimators, including biased ones.
cards.prompt: State a finite-variance Lehmann-Scheffe theorem and its uniqueness/comparator scope.
required_concepts: S is complete and sufficient.
delta(S) is unbiased with finite second moments under the model laws.
Conclude UMVU and almost-sure uniqueness within the unbiased finite-variance class.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A measurable selection from the parameter values maximizing observed likelihood with nonexistence nonuniqueness boundaries and nuisance handling explicit.
major_error_concepts: Solving the interior score equation and ignoring boundaries or multiple maximizers.
cards.prompt: Define Maximum-likelihood estimator. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A measurable selection from the parameter values maximizing observed likelihood with nonexistence nonuniqueness boundaries and nuisance handling explicit.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The expected squared distance from estimator to target decomposing into variance plus squared bias in the scalar squared-error case.
major_error_concepts: Comparing only variance and ignoring changed bias or target scaling.
cards.prompt: Define Mean-squared estimation error. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The expected squared distance from estimator to target decomposing into variance plus squared bias in the scalar squared-error case.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The solution obtained by equating declared empirical moments to model moments with identification multiplicity and admissible roots controlled.
major_error_concepts: Selecting one numerical root without checking parameter constraints or uniqueness.
cards.prompt: Define Method-of-moments estimator. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The solution obtained by equating declared empirical moments to model moments with identification multiplicity and admissible roots controlled.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The property that an MLE of a transformed target is obtained by transforming likelihood maximizers with many-to-one cases treated as an image set.
major_error_concepts: Confusing estimator transformation invariance with coordinate-invariant bias or risk.
cards.prompt: Define MLE transformation invariance. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The property that an MLE of a transformed target is obtained by transforming likelihood maximizers with many-to-one cases treated as an image set.

cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It lower-bounds an unbiased estimator's covariance matrix using the inverse Fisher-information geometry and supports efficiency comparisons; regularity, unbiasedness, parameterization, and nonsingularity conditions matter.
major_error_concepts: Comparing matrices entrywise or inverting a singular information matrix silently.
cards.prompt: What is Multiparameter information inequality used for, and what is its main limitation?
required_concepts: It lower-bounds an unbiased estimator's covariance matrix using the inverse Fisher-information geometry and supports efficiency comparisons
regularity, unbiasedness, parameterization, and nonsingularity conditions matter.

cards.definition: In a regular p-parameter model with nonsingular Fisher information I(theta), let T be an unbiased q-vector estimator of differentiable g(theta), with finite covariance and valid score/interchange identities. If J_g is the q-by-p target Jacobian, Cov_theta(T) - J_g I(theta)^(-1) J_g^T is positive semidefinite. This is a quadratic-form ordering, not an entrywise lower bound; sample information and parameterization must be consistent.
major_error_concepts: The covariance bound means every off-diagonal covariance must numerically exceed the corresponding inverse-information entry.
cards.prompt: State the multiparameter information inequality for an unbiased vector target, including the matrix ordering.
required_concepts: Use a finite-covariance unbiased vector estimator and regular nonsingular information.
State Cov(T)≥J_g I^(-1) J_g^T in PSD order.
Give the Jacobian orientation or an equivalent consistent convention.

cards.definition: Partition theta=(psi,eta) into target and nuisance coordinates and partition regular Fisher information conformably. If I_eta_eta is invertible, efficient target information is I_eff=I_psi_psi-I_psi_eta I_eta_eta^(-1) I_eta_psi. It is the covariance of the target score after its linear projection on nuisance scores is removed. Under full nonsingularity, the target covariance bound uses I_eff^(-1), not I_psi_psi^(-1) as if eta were known.
major_error_concepts: Unknown nuisance parameters can always be ignored by using only I_psi_psi as the efficient information.
cards.prompt: Give the nuisance-adjusted efficient-information formula from a partitioned Fisher matrix.
required_concepts: State the nuisance-block Schur complement with consistent block order.
It removes the nuisance-score projection.
Distinguish unknown-nuisance information from the known-nuisance target block.

cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It improves or preserves a convex-loss risk by conditioning an estimator on a sufficient statistic, providing a systematic variance-reduction move; strict improvement is not guaranteed and the target estimand remains unchanged.
major_error_concepts: Conditioning on an arbitrary statistic or claiming strict improvement when the estimator was already measurable from it.
cards.prompt: What is Rao-Blackwell improvement theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
required_concepts: It improves or preserves a convex-loss risk by conditioning an estimator on a sufficient statistic, providing a systematic variance-reduction move
strict improvement is not guaranteed and the target estimand remains unchanged.

cards.definition: Let S be sufficient and T an integrable estimator taking values in a convex action space such that T*=E_theta[T|S] has a parameter-free version in that action space. For loss convex in the action and well-defined risks, Jensen gives R(theta,T*)≤R(theta,T) for every theta. Unbiasedness is preserved. Under squared loss and finite second moments, the variance reduction is E_theta[Var_theta(T|S)], so improvement is strict only when that quantity is positive.
major_error_concepts: Conditioning always strictly improves risk, even when the estimator is already a function of S.
cards.prompt: State the Rao-Blackwell theorem and its strictness boundary.
required_concepts: Define the improved estimator by conditional expectation given a sufficient statistic.
State the convex-loss risk inequality with existence/integrability conditions.
Unbiasedness is preserved and strict improvement is not guaranteed.

cards.definition: **Definition.** In a regular scalar model, every unbiased estimator T of g(theta) satisfies Var_theta(T)>=[g'(theta)]^2/I_n(theta), provided the support and differentiation-under-the-integral conditions hold and 0<I_n(theta)<infinity.
major_error_concepts: Applying the bound to a support-dependent uniform family where regular score identities fail.
cards.prompt: Define Scalar Cramer-Rao inequality. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: T is unbiased for g(theta) in a regular scalar model.
Var_theta(T)>=[g'(theta)]^2/I_n(theta).
Support, interchange, and finite positive information conditions are required.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An unbiased estimator with variance no larger than every other unbiased estimator for each parameter value under the specified target and model.
major_error_concepts: Calling UMVU minimax or optimal among biased estimators under every loss.
cards.prompt: Define UMVU estimator. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An unbiased estimator with variance no larger than every other unbiased estimator for each parameter value under the specified target and model.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The set of allowed terminal decisions predictions estimates or sets kept distinct from the parameter space even when the two happen to coincide.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every parameter value is an allowed action or omitting abstention constraints.
cards.prompt: Define Action space. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The set of allowed terminal decisions predictions estimates or sets kept distinct from the parameter space even when the two happen to coincide.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The inequality that every prior Bayes risk lower-bounds worst-case risk and can certify minimaxity when matched by a rule's maximum risk.
major_error_concepts: Using one rule's integrated risk as a lower bound on all rules.
cards.prompt: Define Bayes lower bound for minimax risk. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The inequality that every prior Bayes risk lower-bounds worst-case risk and can certify minimaxity when matched by a rule's maximum risk.

cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It uniformly controls the empirical distribution function around the population CDF without distributional shape assumptions, enabling confidence bands and sample guarantees; the bound concerns iid scalar observations and may be conservative.
major_error_concepts: Applying it to dependent observations or calling the bound an exact coverage equality.
cards.prompt: What is Distribution-free DKW inequality used for, and what is its main limitation?
required_concepts: It uniformly controls the empirical distribution function around the population CDF without distributional shape assumptions, enabling confidence bands and sample guarantees
the bound concerns iid scalar observations and may be conservative.

cards.definition: For iid real observations with CDF F and empirical CDF F_n, P(sup_x|F_n(x)-F(x)|>epsilon)≤2 exp(-2n epsilon²) for epsilon>0. No continuity of F is required. With epsilon_alpha=sqrt(log(2/alpha)/(2n)), the band [max(0,F_n-epsilon_alpha), min(1,F_n+epsilon_alpha)] covers F simultaneously for all x with probability at least 1-alpha. This is a coverage lower bound, not an exact equality.
major_error_concepts: DKW gives an exact 1-alpha pointwise interval with width sqrt(log(2/alpha))/n for arbitrary dependent data.
cards.prompt: State the two-sided DKW-Massart inequality and invert it into a simultaneous CDF confidence band.
required_concepts: Use iid scalar observations and the supremum over all thresholds.
Give the two-sided bound 2 exp(-2n epsilon²).
Invert it to the simultaneous band width sqrt(log(2/alpha)/(2n)).

cards.definition: **Definition.** For observations X_1 through X_n, the empirical cumulative distribution function is F_n(x)=n^{-1} sum_{i=1}^n 1{X_i<=x}, the right-continuous cumulative function of the empirical probability measure.
major_error_concepts: Naming only the equal-mass empirical measure or bootstrap resampling law without defining the cumulative function of x.
cards.prompt: Define Empirical cumulative distribution function.
required_concepts: For observations X_1 through X_n, the empirical cumulative distribution function is F_n(x)=n^{-1} sum_{i=1}^n 1{X_i<=x},
the right-continuous cumulative function of the empirical probability measure.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The latent-variable iteration alternating posterior expectation of complete-data log likelihood and parameter maximization with observed-likelihood monotonicity and local-optimum limits explicit.
major_error_concepts: Calling every stationary point the global MLE or comparing runs without label and initialization control.
cards.prompt: Define Expectation-maximization algorithm. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The latent-variable iteration alternating posterior expectation of complete-data log likelihood
and parameter maximization with observed-likelihood monotonicity and local-optimum limits explicit.

cards.definition: If X_i are iid real observations with CDF F and F_n(x)=n^(-1)sum_i 1{X_i≤x}, then sup_{x in R}|F_n(x)-F(x)|→0 almost surely. This is uniform consistency over thresholds, valid even with atoms. It is not a finite-n confidence level or a root-n limiting-distribution statement.
major_error_concepts: Pointwise convergence at each threshold is the entire Glivenko-Cantelli conclusion, with no sampling assumptions.
cards.prompt: State the classical empirical-CDF Glivenko-Cantelli theorem and its sampling assumptions.
required_concepts: Use iid real observations and their empirical CDF.
State almost-sure convergence of the supremum CDF error to zero.
Distinguish uniform consistency from finite-sample bands or a CLT.

cards.definition: For a square-integrable symmetric order-m kernel with theta=E[h], define canonical projections h_j by conditional expectation and subtraction of all lower-order projections; for example h_1(x)=E[h(x,X_2,...,X_m)]-theta. Then U_n-theta=sum_{j=1}^m binom(m,j) U_(n,j)(h_j), where each h_j is conditionally mean-zero in any one argument and components of different order are orthogonal in L² under iid sampling. The leading term is (m/n)sum_i h_1(X_i). If its variance vanishes, the usual nondegenerate root-n CLT is not available automatically.
major_error_concepts: The leading term always has nonzero variance, so every U-statistic has a nondegenerate root-n normal limit.
cards.prompt: State the Hoeffding projection decomposition of an iid U-statistic and the role of its first projection.
required_concepts: State the first projection and its coefficient m/n in the leading sum.
Higher canonical projections are degenerate and orthogonal across orders.
A zero first projection changes the leading asymptotic analysis.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The systematic recomputation after deleting each independent unit used for bias and variance approximation with smoothness and unit structure explicit.
major_error_concepts: Deleting individual rows from clustered data or applying smooth-function formulas to a nonsmooth statistic without checking.
cards.prompt: Define Jackknife leave-one-out approximation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The systematic recomputation after deleting each independent unit used for bias and variance approximation with smoothness and unit structure explicit.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The conditional empirical distribution of a statistic recomputed on iid draws with replacement from the empirical law using original sampling units.
major_error_concepts: Sampling without replacement or resampling rows when clusters are the independent units.
cards.prompt: Define Nonparametric bootstrap law. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The conditional empirical distribution of a statistic recomputed on iid draws with replacement from the empirical law using original sampling units.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The inconsistency that can occur for boundary extreme selection or nonregular functionals even with infinitely many resamples from the empirical law.
major_error_concepts: Increasing replicate count and claiming the structural failure is repaired.
cards.prompt: Define Nonsmooth-bootstrap failure. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The inconsistency that can occur for boundary extreme selection or nonregular functionals even with infinitely many resamples from the empirical law.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The conditional simulation of new samples from a fitted parametric model followed by refitting or recomputing the target procedure.
major_error_concepts: Calling the result model-free or holding fitted nuisance values fixed when the procedure normally re-estimates them.
cards.prompt: Define Parametric bootstrap law. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The conditional simulation of new samples from a fitted parametric model followed by refitting or recomputing the target procedure.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The finite-sample randomization validity obtained by comparing a statistic over a transformation group under a null invariance or exchangeability law.
major_error_concepts: Permuting nonexchangeable time or clustered labels and calling the p-value exact.
cards.prompt: Define Permutation-test exactness. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The finite-sample randomization validity obtained by comparing a statistic over a transformation group under a null invariance or exchangeability law.

cards.definition: For iid real observations, fix p in (0,1) and a unique population p-quantile q_p. If F has a continuous positive density f near q_p, then an ordinary sample p-quantile qhat_p satisfies sqrt(n)(qhat_p-q_p)⇒N(0,p(1-p)/f(q_p)²). This concerns a fixed interior probability level and regular quantile, not an extreme order statistic, atom, or zero-density quantile.
major_error_concepts: The asymptotic quantile variance is p(1-p)f(q_p)² and remains valid at a point mass.
cards.prompt: State the asymptotic distribution of a regular fixed-probability sample quantile.
required_concepts: Use iid sampling, fixed interior p, and a unique regular quantile.
Require continuous positive density at the quantile.
State the root-n normal limit with variance p(1-p)/f(q_p)².

cards.definition: **Definition.** A statistic depending on sample ordering rather than raw magnitudes with tie handling and distribution-free null claims qualified.
major_error_concepts: Claiming ranks remove every distribution assumption or ignoring ties and group-size conditioning.
cards.prompt: Define Rank statistic. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A statistic depending on sample ordering rather than raw magnitudes with tie handling and distribution-free null claims qualified.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An order-statistic or inverse empirical-CDF estimator under a declared probability level and tie interpolation convention.
major_error_concepts: Switching software quantile conventions and treating results as identical.
cards.prompt: Define Sample quantile. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An order-statistic or inverse empirical-CDF estimator under a declared probability level and tie interpolation convention.

cards.definition: For iid continuous differences D_i, the sign test uses S=sum_i 1{D_i>0}; under P(D_i>0)=1/2 it has Binomial(n,1/2) law. The Wilcoxon signed-rank statistic sums ranks of |D_i| for positive D_i; its usual exact null uses a continuous distribution symmetric about zero, so signs are independent fair signs conditional on magnitudes. Ties/zeros need a declared treatment. Neither is a distribution-free mean test for arbitrary asymmetric laws.
major_error_concepts: Signed-rank and sign tests have identical exact assumptions and both test any population mean without symmetry.
cards.prompt: Distinguish the sign and Wilcoxon signed-rank statistics and their usual exact-null assumptions.
required_concepts: The sign statistic counts positives and uses a fair-sign null.
Signed ranks weight positives by absolute-difference ranks and require the usual symmetry condition.
Qualify zeros/ties and do not equate either procedure with an unrestricted mean test.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The numerical evaluation of products sums log-sum-exp constraints derivatives and stopping criteria while preserving the exact likelihood objective and approximation receipt.
major_error_concepts: Changing the objective by clipping probabilities or dropping small components without declaring approximation.
cards.prompt: Define Stable log-likelihood computation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The numerical evaluation of products sums log-sum-exp constraints derivatives
and stopping criteria while preserving the exact likelihood objective and approximation receipt.

cards.definition: For iid X_1,...,X_n and a symmetric integrable kernel h of fixed order m≤n, U_n=binom(n,m)^(-1)sum_{1≤i_1<...<i_m≤n}h(X_i1,...,X_im). Its expectation is theta=E[h(X_1,...,X_m)]. The average is over distinct unordered subsets; an equivalent ordered-tuple formula needs its matching normalization. Terms overlap and are not generally independent.
major_error_concepts: A U-statistic averages all n^m tuples including repeated indices, and those terms are iid.
cards.prompt: Define a U-statistic of fixed kernel order m, with normalization and unbiased target.
required_concepts: Give the distinct-index kernel average with correct normalization.
The iid symmetric integrable kernel targets its expectation without bias.
Overlapping tuple terms need not be independent.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The smallest contamination fraction capable of driving an estimator arbitrarily far or outside a declared bounded parameter region with replacement and finite-sample conventions explicit.
major_error_concepts: Equating bounded influence with a high breakdown point.
cards.prompt: Define Breakdown point. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: First material clause: The smallest contamination fraction capable of driving an estimator arbitrarily far or outside
Remaining material clause: a declared bounded parameter region with replacement and finite-sample conventions explicit.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The neighborhood of distributions formed by mixing a nominal model with an unspecified contaminating law at a bounded fraction with target and adversary class explicit.
major_error_concepts: Calling a few deleted outliers a formal robustness guarantee.
cards.prompt: Define Contamination robustness model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: First material clause: The neighborhood of distributions formed by mixing a nominal model with an unspecified
Remaining material clause: contaminating law at a bounded fraction with target and adversary class explicit.

cards.definition: Let J be uniform on M≥2 hypotheses and let X have law P_J. With natural logarithms, every decoder has P(Jhat≠J)≥1-[I(J;X)+log 2]/log M, optionally replaced by zero if negative. If the corresponding parameters have pairwise metric distance at least 2 delta, nearest-point decoding yields squared-metric minimax risk at least delta² times this nonnegative bound. The information concerns the full observed sample; a large packing without a small-information argument gives no useful conclusion.
major_error_concepts: Any large collection of well-separated parameters proves large estimation risk even when the data reveal the hypothesis index perfectly.
cards.prompt: State an entropy-form Fano lower bound and explain the squared-metric packing-to-risk reduction.
required_concepts: Give the entropy-form error bound using mutual information and log M.
Require separated parameter hypotheses to turn error into squared-distance risk.
Use the full sample information and a nonnegative version of the bound.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The weighted estimator using draws from a proposal and target-to-proposal density ratios with support finite-moment and self-normalization bias qualifications.
major_error_concepts: Reversing the weights or claiming finite variance from a large nominal sample count.
cards.prompt: Define Importance-sampling posterior estimator. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The weighted estimator using draws from a proposal and target-to-proposal density ratios with support finite-moment and self-normalization bias qualifications.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The first-order derivative of a statistical functional under infinitesimal point-mass contamination with boundedness interpretation and model location explicit.
major_error_concepts: Treating an observed leave-one-out change as the population influence function without scaling and limit.
cards.prompt: Define Influence function. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The first-order derivative of a statistical functional under infinitesimal point-mass contamination with boundedness interpretation and model location explicit.

cards.definition: For two observation laws P0,P1, the minimum equal-prior testing error is [1-TV(P0,P1)]/2, with TV=sup_B|P0(B)-P1(B)|. If corresponding parameters are separated by metric distance Delta, nearest-parameter decoding gives the squared-metric minimax-risk lower bound Delta²[1-TV(P0,P1)]/8. The laws must describe the entire observed sample, such as product laws for iid data. This stated testing-reduction constant is a valid bound, not a claim of the sharpest possible quadratic-loss constant.
major_error_concepts: Parameter separation alone proves a risk lower bound even when the two full-sample laws have disjoint supports and are perfectly distinguishable.
cards.prompt: State Le Cam's two-law testing identity and a squared-metric estimation lower bound obtained from it.
required_concepts: State the equal-prior testing error in terms of 1-TV.
Include parameter separation and the declared squared-loss constant in the estimation reduction.
Compute distances between full observation laws, not blindly between single-observation laws.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The transition kernel stationarity irreducibility recurrence and initialization conditions linking a Markov-chain sample to the posterior target with convergence mode declared.
major_error_concepts: Calling accepted proposals iid posterior samples or using trace appearance as proof of convergence.
cards.prompt: Define MCMC invariant-target contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The transition kernel stationarity irreducibility recurrence
and initialization conditions linking a Markov-chain sample to the posterior target with convergence mode declared.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The uncertainty of an ergodic average governed by autocorrelation effective sample size and chain central-limit conditions rather than nominal iterations alone.
major_error_concepts: Dividing sample variance by total iterations as if draws were independent.
cards.prompt: Define MCMC Monte Carlo error. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The uncertainty of an ergodic average governed by autocorrelation effective sample size and chain central-limit conditions rather than nominal iterations alone.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The exact posterior expectation probability quantile predictive law or Bayes action being approximated with normalization parameterization and numerical tolerance explicit.
major_error_concepts: Running a sampler without identifying which posterior functional its output estimates.
cards.prompt: Define Posterior computation target. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: First material clause: The exact posterior expectation probability quantile predictive law or Bayes action
Remaining material clause: being approximated with normalization parameterization and numerical tolerance explicit.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The model parameter minimizing population discrepancy or expected negative log likelihood when no candidate law equals the data law with target shift explicit.
major_error_concepts: Using MLE consistency language while silently retaining the original scientific parameter target.
cards.prompt: Define Pseudo-true parameter under misspecification. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The model parameter minimizing population discrepancy or expected negative log likelihood when no candidate law equals the data law with target shift explicit.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The bounded or redescending estimating function defining a location or regression functional with Fisher consistency tuning and multiple-root behavior explicit.
major_error_concepts: Calling bounded residual contribution proof of global breakdown resistance.
cards.prompt: Define Robust M-estimating score. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The bounded or redescending estimating function defining a location or regression functional with Fisher consistency tuning and multiple-root behavior explicit.

cards.definition: For iid units and a consistent root of n^(-1)sum_i psi(X_i,theta)=0 at a target with E[psi(X,theta0)]=0, let A=E[partial psi/partial theta^T] be nonsingular and B=E[psi psi^T] finite. Under a valid Taylor expansion and CLT, sqrt(n)(theta_hat-theta0)⇒N(0,A^(-1) B A^(-T)). The estimator covariance is approximately that sandwich divided by n. Robust covariance does not change an incorrect target into the desired scientific estimand.
major_error_concepts: Sandwich covariance is A B A and remains exact for arbitrary dependent units without adapting B.
cards.prompt: State the estimating-equation sandwich covariance formula and its sample-size convention.
required_concepts: Define the derivative matrix A and score covariance B under iid moment conditions.
Use A^(-1) B A^(-T) for the root-n limit covariance.
Divide by n for estimator covariance and do not claim target correctness from a covariance repair.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The invalidity caused when the same data choose a model target hypothesis or reporting subset and standard post-selection calibration ignores that event.
major_error_concepts: Calling multiplicity adjustment alone a complete repair for arbitrary adaptive selection.
cards.prompt: Define Selection-induced inference failure. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The invalidity caused when the same data choose a model target hypothesis or reporting subset and standard post-selection calibration ignores that event.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The distinction between a procedure designed with anytime or sequential error guarantees and an ordinary fixed-sample test whose calibration can fail under adaptive stopping.
major_error_concepts: Claiming optional stopping never matters or that a martingale name alone supplies the desired error control.
cards.prompt: Define Sequential optional-stopping boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The distinction between a procedure designed with anytime or sequential error guarantees
and an ordinary fixed-sample test whose calibration can fail under adaptive stopping.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The accumulating likelihood-ratio procedure with upper and lower stopping boundaries error guarantees and expected-sample claims tied to simple hypotheses and overshoot qualifications.
major_error_concepts: Peeking repeatedly at a fixed-sample p-value and calling it an SPRT.
cards.prompt: Define Sequential probability-ratio test. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The accumulating likelihood-ratio procedure with upper and lower stopping boundaries error guarantees
and expected-sample claims tied to simple hypotheses and overshoot qualifications.
